foods.name: Cooked Rice
foods.question: How Long Does Cooked Rice Last in the Fridge?
foods.answer: USDA's FoodKeeper lists cooked rice at 4 to 6 days in the refrigerator. Its general entry for leftovers without meat, which names rice, is shorter: 3 to 4 days.
foods.freezer_answer: Yes. FoodKeeper lists cooked rice at 6 months in the freezer, and leftovers without meat at 1 to 2 months.
foods.index_summary: 4 to 6 days in the refrigerator

tips.heading: Refrigerate within 2 hours
tips.text: Never leave food out of refrigeration over 2 hours. If the temperature is above 90°F, make it 1 hour.

tips.heading: Use shallow containers
tips.text: Put leftovers in shallow containers so they cool quickly, and refrigerate them at 40°F or below.

tips.heading: Reheat to 165°F
tips.text: Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 165°F, or until hot and steaming. In the microwave, cover the food and rotate it so it heats evenly.

foods.name: Cooked Pasta
foods.question: How Long Does Cooked Pasta Last, and Can You Freeze It?
foods.answer: Cooked pasta keeps 3 to 5 days in the refrigerator, according to USDA's FoodKeeper.
foods.freezer_answer: Yes. FoodKeeper lists cooked pasta at 1 to 2 months in the freezer. Pasta salad is different: freezing is not recommended.
foods.index_summary: 3 to 5 days in the refrigerator

tips.heading: Refrigerate within 2 hours
tips.text: Never leave food out of refrigeration over 2 hours. If the temperature is above 90°F, make it 1 hour.

tips.heading: Cover or seal it
tips.text: Cover leftovers, wrap them in airtight packaging, or seal them in storage containers. That keeps bacteria out, holds in moisture, and stops them picking up odors from other food.

tips.heading: No need to thaw first
tips.text: It is safe to reheat frozen leftovers without thawing them. It takes longer than reheating thawed food.

foods.name: Cooked Chicken
foods.question: How Long Does Cooked Chicken Last in the Fridge?
foods.answer: Cooked chicken keeps 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator, according to USDA's FoodKeeper. That covers cooked poultry dishes, fried chicken, and a rotisserie chicken counted from the day you buy it.
foods.freezer_answer: Yes. FoodKeeper lists cooked poultry dishes at 4 to 6 months in the freezer, and fried or rotisserie chicken at 4 months.
foods.index_summary: 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator

foods.name: Deli Meat
foods.question: How Long Is Deli Meat Good For?
foods.answer: Deli meat sliced at the store keeps 3 to 5 days in the refrigerator from the date of purchase. Pre-packaged lunch meat keeps 2 weeks from the date of purchase, then 3 to 5 days after opening. Those are USDA FoodKeeper times.
foods.freezer_answer: Yes. FoodKeeper lists both store-sliced and pre-packaged lunch meat at 1 to 2 months in the freezer.
foods.index_summary: 2 weeks sealed, 3 to 5 days once opened or store-sliced

foods.name: Eggs
foods.question: How Long Do Eggs Last in the Fridge?
foods.answer: Raw eggs in the shell keep 3 to 5 weeks in the refrigerator from the date of purchase, according to USDA's FoodKeeper.
foods.freezer_answer: Not in the shell: FoodKeeper marks freezing as not recommended for eggs in the shell. Raw whites and yolks are listed at 12 months in the freezer.
foods.index_summary: 3 to 5 weeks in the refrigerator, in the shell

tips.heading: Chill it right away
tips.text: Refrigerate or freeze ground beef as soon as possible after purchase. That preserves freshness and slows the growth of bacteria.

tips.heading: Cook it to 160°F
tips.text: Cook ground beef to a safe minimum internal temperature of 160°F, measured with a food thermometer. FoodKeeper lists the same temperature.

tips.heading: Thaw it in the fridge

foods.name: Raw Chicken
foods.question: How Long Does Raw Chicken Last in the Fridge?
foods.answer: Raw chicken keeps 1 to 2 days in the refrigerator from the date of purchase, whole or in parts, according to USDA's FoodKeeper.
foods.freezer_answer: Yes. FoodKeeper lists a whole chicken at 12 months in the freezer, chicken parts at 9 months, and ground chicken at 3 to 4 months, all from the date of purchase.
foods.index_summary: 1 to 2 days in the refrigerator from the date of purchase

foodkeeper_cooking.tip: Cooking times for poultry are for unstuffed birds. Check the internal temperature in the innermost part of the thigh, innermost part of the wing, and thickest part of the breast. Add 15 to 30 minutes for stuffed birds. Stuffed birds are ready when the internal temperature of stuffing reaches 165°F.
Cooking suggestions are for burgers. Cooking times are per side if grilling.

tips.heading: Don't wash it
tips.text: Washing raw poultry before cooking is not recommended, because bacteria in the juices can spread to other foods, utensils, and surfaces. Only cooking destroys them.

kepta_bridge.source: Kepta app catalog, checked by the Kepta chat on 2026-11-25. These are Kepta refrigerator or pantry dates, not USDA figures.

tips.heading: The fridge is for quality
tips.text: FoodKeeper says shelf-stable commercial salsa is safe at room temperature after opening. Refrigerating it is about keeping it fresh longer, not safety.

tips.heading: Fresh salsa is different
tips.text: FoodKeeper gives fresh and homemade fresh salsa a refrigerator time only, with no pantry time.

tips.heading: Trust the signs of spoilage
tips.text: Spoiled foods develop an off odor, flavor, or texture. If a food has developed those characteristics, it should not be eaten.

foods.name: Bread
foods.question: How Long Does Bread Last?
foods.answer: Commercial bread keeps 14 to 18 days in the pantry from the date of purchase, according to USDA's FoodKeeper. It lists commercially baked, pre-sliced whole wheat bread at a shorter 3 to 5 days.
foods.freezer_answer: Yes. FoodKeeper lists commercial bread at 3 to 5 months in the freezer from the date of purchase, and whole wheat bread at 3 months.
foods.index_summary: 14 to 18 days in the pantry from the date of purchase

kepta_bridge.text: Kepta’s date for bread is shorter than USDA’s: 7 days in the pantry for any loaf, because bread at home often goes stale or moldy before 14. For a whole wheat loaf, USDA’s 3 to 5 days is the safer guide. A date you set yourself always wins.

tips.heading: The fridge dries it out
tips.text: For pre-sliced whole wheat bread, FoodKeeper does not recommend refrigeration: the bread will quickly dry out and become stale.

tips.heading: Mold means the loaf goes
tips.text: USDA says to discard bread and baked goods that show mold. Porous foods can be contaminated below the surface.

tips.heading: Bread can sit out
tips.text: USDA names bread as an exception to the rule that food left at room temperature for more than 2 hours should be discarded.
